reviews.title: Infinigen Indoors
reviews.reason: Reusable procedural asset+constraint code, controlled solver ablations and downstream annotation tests justify sustained reading. The actual random-sample image supports adequate static scene quality; recommendation excludes uninspected contact/robot execution.
reviews.material_difference: Unlike Holodeck's fixed retrieved asset library, geometry and materials are procedural and editable down to asset parameters; dense annotations and solver controls are the retained value.

inspection_evidence.locator: Full official random-sample grid: top-left dining, top-right living room, bottom-left bathroom and bottom-right kitchen quadrants, including thumbnail strips
inspection_evidence.observation: The four main room groups have recognizable furniture/cabinet/sanitary fixtures, coherent wall/floor perspective and lighting, and visibly varied room arrangements in thumbnail strips. Geometry appears coherent in these rendered views; some surfaces and objects are visually simple.
inspection_evidence.coverage: Multiple static rooms and layouts in one official sample grid; adequate static PCG/annotation quality.
inspection_evidence.limitations: Only rendered images inspected. Occluded mesh topology, articulation, physical contacts, long-tail generation failure and robot execution are unverified and excluded from the recommendation.

sources.claim: §3.2/3.4 details constraint DSL and export; §4.1/Table3 ablates solver; §4.3/Table4 validates occlusion-boundary training.

Reusable constraint/annotation/export infrastructure. Solver ablation uses20 scenes/5K steps; occlusion-boundary comparison trains matched U-Nets. These are author-reported controls, not independently reproduced robotics validation.
